WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Little Deer’s Story Paths Worksheet for Age 4

Rain at the window — choose the story path: watch the rain, take the umbrella, open it, and out for a walk.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

A choose-the-path story: at each fork one choice keeps the rainy day sensible and one flies off to the beach or the snow. Because each choice changes the story, the sheet begs to be played twice — once sensible, once deliberately silly, with a retelling of both.

  • Story-path choosing
  • Keeping a story sensible
  • Weather reasoning
  • Retelling a chosen path

On the sheet: Follow the pictures in the right story order!

WHERE THIS FITS

The class behind it.

This worksheet belongs to Storytime & Pre-Reading Comprehension (Class 29) on the Age 4 learning path, and the whole reading collection lives at /worksheets/reading/. One finished sheet is a full session — download it, print it, and let the fridge door be the gallery.

PRINT & PLAY ON PAPER

Take it to the table.

The PDF is a real printable file (A4, prints fine on US Letter). The print button opens the same PDF ready to print — nothing stored.

HOW TO USE IT

Three easy steps.

  1. Tell the story together

    Read the title and instruction aloud, then let your child point at the picture and say what happens. The picture carries the whole activity — no reading needed.

  2. Mark the picture, then retell

    Circle, number or draw on the sheet exactly as the game plays on screen. Afterwards ask “can you tell me the whole story?” — the retelling is the comprehension.

  3. Use the draw box

    Every sheet ends with room to draw the next part of the story. A drawing plus one spoken sentence is a complete session.

TEACHING TIPS

Little things that help.

Wrong answers are information

If the story comes out in the wrong order, retell it together and try again tomorrow. Comprehension grows from talking, not from being right first time.

Say the WHY out loud

“Why does Rabbit need the umbrella?” Asking for the reason turns a matching task into real story thinking.

Print it twice

Once to do, once to keep. Children love redoing a favorite story a week later and feeling how easy it got.

Answer guide

The A path all the way: watch the rain → take the umbrella → open it → walk in the rain. The B choices (beach, goggles, snowman) don’t fit a rainy day.
